originalTitle: US stock: S&P 500 ends lower as investors weigh data, Middle East tensions
simplifiedContent: The S&P 500, a key stock market index, fell in value after a long period of growth. This happened because sales at stores and online were not as strong as expected, which made investors a bit worried about how people are spending their money. Some stocks, like Applied Materials, also did poorly, which affected other similar stocks. On the other hand, energy companies did well because oil prices are rising. This mix of good and bad news reflects the current uncertainty in the market, with some stocks doing well and others not.

originalTitle: Nvidia’s $500 billion plan envelops Wall Street in its AI frenzy
simplifiedContent: Nvidia, a big tech company, has announced a huge plan to help other companies that work with artificial intelligence (AI). The plan, worth $500 billion, aims to provide money to these companies so they can buy special AI computer chips. Nvidia is working with big banks and financial institutions to make this happen. This plan matters because many companies need a lot of computing power to develop and use AI, and Nvidia's plan can help them get the resources they need. By doing this, Nvidia hopes to support the growth of the tech industry and the development of AI technology.

originalTitle: How a $900 million bet on SpaceX turned 100x into $94 billion for Alphabet
simplifiedContent: Alphabet, the company that owns Google, invested $900 million in the space company SpaceX. This investment has grown a huge amount and is now worth around $94 billion, which is about 100 times the original amount. This means Alphabet's investment in SpaceX has been very successful and they now own the largest share of the company. Other big investors, like Fidelity and Saudi Arabia's investment fund, also have significant stakes in SpaceX. This matters because it shows that Alphabet's investment decision was very good and has led to a huge increase in the value of their stake in the company.

originalTitle: Oil Rises as US Warns of More Economic Pressure to Isolate Iran
simplifiedContent: The price of oil has gone up a bit because the US is threatening to take strong economic actions against Iran. This warning is making traders (people who buy and sell oil) think that there might be less oil available, which is why the price is rising. There's already been a war going on near the Strait of Hormuz, a important route for oil transportation, for six months. This situation is causing uncertainty and tension, which is affecting the oil market. The threat of more economic pressure on Iran is adding to the uncertainty, which is why oil prices are increasing.

originalTitle: Dollar falls on surprise drop in US retail sales
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar has gone down because of a surprise decrease in the amount of things people bought in stores in the US. This decrease in retail sales was not expected, which means it caught investors off guard. As a result, the dollar's value fell compared to other currencies. This matters because a weaker dollar can affect how much things cost in the US and how well American businesses do. The drop in retail sales is important because it can give investors an idea of how the US economy is doing.

originalTitle: Patanjali Foods shares to be in focus on Monday as Q1 net profit jumps 86%; revenue hits record
simplifiedContent: Patanjali Foods, a company listed on the stock market, had a very good quarter from April to June. The company's profit increased by 86% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹335.73 crore. The company also made a record amount of money, ₹11,337.45 crore, during this time. This news is important because it might affect the price of Patanjali Foods' shares on Monday. The company has also decided to give its shareholders a 40% dividend, which is a portion of the company's profit.
